item.title: RT NHAI: As part of its continued efforts to improve cleanliness and maintenance of toilet facilities along National Highways, NHAI has introduced a s...
item.description:
RT NHAI
As part of its continued efforts to improve cleanliness and maintenance of toilet facilities along National Highways, NHAI has introduced a stricter monitoring and enforcement mechanism. The new measures will ensure proper upkeep and maintenance of toilet blocks and other facilities, including toll collection booths, surrounding areas and signboards.

User Fee Collection Agencies will be required to comply with the prescribed service standards for toilets and other facilities. Under the new mechanism, NHAI officials will inspect these facilities at least once every week. If any deficiency is found, the concerned User Fee Collection Agency will be issued a show-cause notice and directed to rectify the issue within the stipulated time.

NHAI has also introduced a provision to take action against agencies that repeatedly fail to rectify deficiencies. If the number of notices for unresolved deficiencies reaches or exceeds 10% of the total number of toll plazas being operated by an agency, the agency will be declared a non-performer. Such an agency will not be eligible to participate in bidding for toll plazas, regular toll plaza contracts, civil works or any other NHAI bid for a period of 15 days or until all pending deficiencies are rectified.

The citizen-centric initiative aims to ensure that agencies responsible for maintaining public-facing infrastructure meet prescribed service standards and address deficiencies promptly.

Read the press release here: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?PRID=2322314®=3&lang=1

VIDEO | Union Minister and JD(U) leader Rajiv Ranjan (Lalan) Singh (@LalanSingh_1) says, "The Congress Party wants to create chaos in the country by attacking constitutional institutions, and it has a history of creating chaos in the country. In 1975, by imposing Emergency, the Congress Party committed an anti-democratic act. Even today, the Congress Party wants to create chaos in the country by attacking constitutional institutions and making unnecessary and objectionable remarks against them. The Congress Party should engage in introspection. Because of its wrong policies, its actions, and the actions of its state governments, the party has been uprooted in states such as West Bengal, Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Haryana, and Maharashtra. The Congress Party has been wiped out in these states. It is merely playing a subordinate role there. The Congress Party has no independent political existence of its own. And today, once again, the Congress Party is targeting constitutional institutions—sometimes the Chief Election Commissioner, sometimes the Election Commission, and sometimes the Supreme Court. These are constitutional institutions; let them do their work. We have also heard that they are taking a petition signed by 10 MPs. If they want to file a petition, then let them file it. The Supreme Court has its own role to perform. Once a petition is filed before the Supreme Court, it will deliver its judgment on the basis of the merits of the case. So, why are they staging a protest in front of the Supreme Court? This is an attempt to discredit constitutional institutions. The Congress Party should engage in introspection and correct its wrong policies. What it is doing now is simply a continuation of those same misguided policies. It is moving in that very direction, proceeding with a negative mindset."

item.description:
VIDEO | Delhi: Indian shooter Neeru Dhanda, who won three medals, including two gold and a silver, at the Asian Games, said the individual gold was the toughest of her three podium finishes, citing the pressure of winning for the country.

Dhanda created history at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games by becoming the first Indian woman to win an individual gold medal in trap shooting. She also won gold in the mixed team event with Kynan Chenai and silver in the women's team event alongside Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer.

"The individual medal was the most difficult for me because there was a lot of pressure to win it for the country. Aside from self-pressure, there is also the pressure of the country, but there is a level of excitement as well that we are here for the country, so the pressure somewhat lessens when you get a source of motivation," Dhanda said.

The 26-year-old, who serves as a Naib Subedar in the Indian Army, said her pride in the country and the armed forces helped her manage the expectations.

(Full video available on PTI Videos - http://ptivideos.com)

VIDEO | INDIA bloc leaders reach Supreme Court.

Congress leader Pawan Khera (@Pawankhera) says, "This is just the beginning. There are many aspects to this fight. One is the legal aspect, another is the political aspect, and the third is the moral aspect. We are fighting on all these fronts. We will fight on the political front as well. On moral grounds too, we will force them to resign."

When asked about denotification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site, he says, "Wherever we gather, the citizens of India are so angry today that wherever they stand becomes Jantar Mantar. Can you de-notify the entire country, no matter how much you try? Tell me. People are angry. What are you de-notifying? Tomorrow, will you de-notify the Constitution as well? I have a constitutional right, brother, to fight and to protest. I am doing so peacefully. Wherever I am standing now, this is Jantar Mantar. Go ahead, de-notify it!"

#ChaloDilliProtest #SupremeCourt #INDIAblocprotest

STORY | 'Hawa hawai leader': Anurag Thakur accuses Rahul of undermining institutions, using theatrics

BJP MP Anurag Thakur on Monday accused Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi of creating instability and chaos in the country, alleging that his actions were aimed at undermining constitutional institutions and tarnishing India's image globally.

In a press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, Thakur said the country had never witnessed such "theatrics and tantrums" from a leader of opposition, whom he described as "destabilising, chaotic and unserious".

Taking a swipe at Gandhi over his repeated allegations of "vote chori", Thakur claimed that the Congress leader was challenging the people's mandate.

"Rahul Gandhi is a 'hawa hawai' leader. His entire style of politics follows the same pattern: 'hawa hawai' – hollow statements, baseless allegations, hollow actions, hollow protests and hollow facts," he alleged.

Today, it has shrunk to just 2,500 acres, and we must protect what remains. The marshland helps protect Chennai from floods by draining water into the Bay of Bengal through the Okkiyam and Buckingham canals. Unfortunately, over the past couple of decades, the marshland has faced encroachment by the Central government, the state government and local authorities. Recently, the DMK government also granted permission for a multi-storey apartment project worth Rs 2,200 crore. We approached the court and opposed the project, which was subsequently struck down."
